answer: A pearl-and-pulse defense: every identity must answer a regular liveness pulse — a fresh, time-bound proof tied to a ferrous hardware root of trust, like a TPM key that cannot be cloned. Each pulse is published and scored; identities that miss pulses lose standing, and new identities start as unproven pearls that earn trust only through a long trail of verified useful work. An attacker minting a thousand fakes must buy a thousand hardware roots and keep every one pulsing on schedule, so each fake costs real silicon, power, and attention instead of a free copy.
